messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Malayalam, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Tant' | Intensifier indicating a high degree of bitterness (so) | Malayalam **അത്ര** (adverb) with emphatic degree; require **adverbial intensifier** preceding the predicate adjective. *Back‑translation check:* “അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ള” → “so bitter”. | | è (1) | Copular verb linking implicit subject “it” to predicate “bitter” | Malayalam **ആണ്** (present copula) agreeing with neuter pronoun **അത്**; required as **present indicative**. *Back‑translation check:* “അത് കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണ്” → “it is bitter”. | | amara | Predicate adjective “bitter” | Malayalam **കയ്പ്പുള്ള** (adjective) in predicative position; must agree in gender‑neutral form. *Back‑translation check:* “കയ്പ്പുള്ള” → “bitter”. | | che | Comparative subordinator “that” introducing clause | Malayalam **എന്നാൽ** (conjunctive) introducing a comparative clause; marks **subordination**. *Back‑translation check:* “എന്നാൽ” → “that”. | | poco | Adverb “little” quantifying the comparative increase | Malayalam **കുറച്ച്** (adverb) placed before comparative marker; required to indicate **small degree**. *Back‑translation check:* “കുറച്ച്” → “little”. | | è (2) | Copular verb in comparative clause linking “death” to “more” | Malayalam **ആണ്** (present copula) with subject **മരണം**; required as **present indicative**. *Back‑translation check:* “മരണം ആണ്” → “death is”. | | più | Comparative adverb “more” indicating higher degree | Malayalam **കൂടുതൽ** (comparative adverb) following **കുറച്ച്**; must encode **comparative direction** (death > bitterness). *Back‑translation check:* “കൂടുതൽ” → “more”. | | morte | Noun “death”, the benchmark of bitterness | Malayalam **മരണം** (noun, neuter) as subject of comparative clause; required in **nominative** case. *Back‑translation check:* “മരണം” → “death”. | | ma | Coordinating conjunction “but” signaling contrast | Malayalam **പക്ഷേ** (conjunctive) linking two clauses; required as **contrastive coordinator**. *Back‑translation check:* “പക്ഷേ” → “but”. | | per | Preposition “in order to” marking purpose | Malayalam **വേണ്ടി** (post‑position) introducing infinitival purpose clause; required with **dative/ablative** case marking. *Back‑translation check:* “വേണ്ടി” → “for / in order to”. | | trattar | Infinitive “to treat/discuss” | Malayalam **ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ** (infinitive verb) with **മൂലവ്യക്തി** (to‑infinitive) form; required after **വേണ്ടി**. *Back‑translation check:* “ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ” → “to discuss”. | | del | Contraction “of the” introducing object of discussion | Malayalam **യുടെ** (genitive case) attached to **നല്ല** (good); required as **genitive marker**. *Back‑translation check:* “യുടെ” → “of”. | | ben | Abstract noun “good” (object of discussion) | Malayalam **നല്ല** (adjective used as noun) in **genitive** after **യുടെ**; required in **neuter/abstract** form. *Back‑translation check:* “നല്ല” → “good”. | | ch'i' | Relative pronoun “that I” introducing clause | Malayalam **ഞാൻ** (first‑person pronoun) + **എന്ന** (relative particle) forming **relative clause**; required to bind clause to **നല്ല**. *Back‑translation check:* “ഞാൻ എന്ന” → “that I”. | | vi | Locative adverb “there” indicating place of discovery | Malayalam **അവിടെ** (adverb of place) placed before verb; required as **locative adverb**. *Back‑translation check:* “അവിടെ” → “there”. | | trovai | Simple past “found” (historic) | Malayalam **കണ്ടു** (past tense verb) with **first‑person singular** agreement; required as **simple past**. *Back‑translation check:* “കണ്ടു” → “found”. | | dirò | Future “I will tell” | Malayalam **പറയാം** (future‑intentional) with **first‑person singular**; required as **future indicative**. *Back‑translation check:* “പറയാം” → “I will tell”. | | de | Preposition “of” introducing domain of discourse | Malayalam **യുടെ** (genitive) attached to **മറ്റു** (other); required as **genitive marker**. *Back‑translation check:* “യുടെ” → “of”. | | l'altre | Determiner + adjective “the other” (plural) | Malayalam **മറ്റു** (adjective) with **plural marker -കൾ** when modifying **വസ്തുക്കൾ**; required as **plural determiner**. *Back‑translation check:* “മറ്റു” → “other”. | | cose | Noun “things” (plural) | Malayalam **വസ്തുക്കൾ** (noun, plural) in **accusative** as object of **പറയാം**; required with **plural suffix -കൾ**. *Back‑translation check:* “വസ്തുക്കൾ” → “things”. | | ch'i' (2) | Relative pronoun “that I” restricting “things” | Malayalam **ഞാൻ** + **എന്ന** forming relative clause; required to modify **വസ്തുക്കൾ**. *Back‑translation check:* “ഞാൻ എന്ന” → “that I”. | | v'ho | Perfect auxiliary “have … there” (locative clitic) | Malayalam **അവിടെ** (locative) + **കണ്ടു** (perfective) combined as **അവിടെ കണ്ടു**; required to express perfect with locative. *Back‑translation check:* “അവിടെ കണ്ടു” → “have seen there”. | | scorte | Past participle “seen” agreeing with “cose” | Malayalam **കണ്ട** (past participle) agreeing in number with **വസ്തുക്കൾ**; required as **agreeing participle**. *Back‑translation check:* “കണ്ട” → “seen”. |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Malayalam components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണ് / അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണു മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് / അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണു
- Line 8: നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ / നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി സംസാരിക്കാൻ / നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി വിശദീകരിക്കാൻ
- Line 9: ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റു വസ്തുക്കൾക്കുറിച്ച് പറയും / ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റു വസ്തുക്കൾക്കുറിച്ച് വിവരിക്കും / ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റു വസ്തുക്കൾക്കുറിച്ച് പറയാൻ പോകുന്നു

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Malayalam lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് എന്ന മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണ്
**Assembly Notes:** - Inserted the complementizer **എന്ന** to link the main predicate with the comparative clause (function‑word only).
**Target Text:** അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് എന്ന മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണ്;
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already encodes purpose and the relative clause.
**Target Text:** നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റു വസ്തുക്കൾക്കുറിച്ച് പറയും
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase expresses future intent, the relative clause, and the object.
**Target Text:** ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റു വസ്തുക്കൾക്കുറിച്ച് പറയും.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Malayalam text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 7 - Target Text (from Step 4): അത്ര കയ്പ്പുള്ളത് എന്ന മരണം കുറച്ച് കൂടുതൽ കയ്പ്പുള്ളതാണ്; - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): So bitter that death is a little more bitter. - Reference Translation (line-aligned): So bitter is it that death is little more. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **OK**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 8 - Target Text (from Step 4): നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ, - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): But to discuss the good that I found there, - Reference Translation (line-aligned): But in order to treat of the good that there I found, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: പക്ഷേ നല്ലയെക്കുറിച്ച് ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ടെത്തിയതിനായി ചർച്ച ചെയ്യാൻ,
- Line #: 9 - Target Text (from Step 4): ഞാൻ അവിടെ കണ്ട മറ്റു വസ്തുക്കൾക്കുറിച്ച് പറയും. - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): I will speak about the other things I saw there. - Reference Translation (line-aligned): I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**FINAL VERIFICATION:** UNVERIFIED (fails on Line 8)
